Subject: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & next steps

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can move toward procurement/security review: 

- Summary: Medwise is evaluating Redwood to support clinical note generation and summarization. During the demo you mentioned the workload will include patient identifiers and clinical notes (so PHI will be processed).

As discussed on the call, here are the important items and questions we need to land on:

1) BAA / PHI eligibility: Redwood offers a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for customers that will process PHI, but PHI cannot be processed on our shared hosted API (public endpoints). Eligible deployment modes for PHI are: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem).

2) PHI boundaries: Can you confirm whether PHI will be included directly in prompts (free-text clinical notes) or only in structured data sent to the model? Also, do attachments (e.g., PDFs/images) contain PHI that will be sent to the model? Clear answers here help us scope the BAA and deployment recommendations.

3) SOC 2 + evidence: I'll share our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a short security questionnaire. Please share your security contact so we can coordinate.

Next steps I propose: I attached our vendor security questionnaire (fill/share what you can), and if you confirm PHI usage we can send an editable BAA draft and start the security review. If you prefer, we can schedule a quick 30-min security sync next week with our security engineer (Dev) and your security/infosec contact.

Attachments: Medwise_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

[p.s. Quick note on deployment eligibility: Hosted API = not eligible for PHI; Dedicated and Private = eligible (we can discuss tradeoffs and timeline).]

Hi Emma —

Short answers:
- Hosted API: not eligible for PHI processing. We cannot sign a BAA for the hosted/public endpoints.
- Options for PHI: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools with customer isolation) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — both support BAAs. Dedicated is usually faster to provision and keeps infrastructure managed by Redwood; Private gives you full network control and can be on-prem if required.

I've attached a draft BAA (redwood_baa_draft.pdf) to start the conversation and the SOC 2 link below. If you confirm you'll process PHI, next steps are: 1) confirm desired deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private), 2) fill the questionnaire and return, 3) we initiate legal/procurement and security review.

SOC 2 (read-only): https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/soc2/redwood_soc2_type2_2025.pdf
Attachments: redwood_baa_draft.pdf, Medwise_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Cc'ing Dev (security) and Neha (solutions) to help with technical/deployment questions.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa / Neha —

Quick internal notes on the Medwise ask:

- Since they confirmed PHI in prompts and real-time requirements, recommend Dedicated as the default (faster onboarding ~2-3 weeks) unless they need on-prem isolation — then Private will be required.

- PHI boundary checklist for procurement/security:
  * Is PHI sent as free-text in prompts, or are identifiers tokenized prior to send?
  * Are there attachments (PDFs/images) that will be OCR'd and forwarded to the model?
  * Retention: what retention window do they require for logs/trace? Redwood can restrict retention for Dedicated/Private per contract (BAA item).
  * Audit logging: we will provide audit logs for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has limited exportability.

Next steps (internal):
- Ask Medwise to confirm data flow (prompts vs structured fields) and retention requirements.
- Send redwood_baa_draft.pdf to legal for initial review and prepare DocuSign route.
- Prepare a one-pager on Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for Marissa to share with the customer.

I can join the security sync if scheduled.

Thanks,
Dev
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

[internal-only note: ensure SOC 2 artifact packaging includes user access lists and key management details before sharing beyond procurement]
